Professional Profile
Investigates how arthropod communities assemble, change, and persist across space and time, combining traditional surveys and collections with
next‑generation sequencing, environmental DNA, and community analysis. Published work addresses forest arthropod turnover and homogenization,
plant–arthropod associations, and retrospective biodiversity monitoring. Current Berkeley work examines how topography, habitat, and invasion
structure Hawaiian arthropod communities. DFG Walter Benjamin Fellow at UC Berkeley with 11 peer‑reviewed publications and research mentoring
across 18 thesis projects.

Arthropod Ecology, Evolution, and Enabling Expertise
Arthropod ecology and
evolution
Hawaiian Cyclosa and Lycosidae, morphological identification, species boundaries, UCE datasets, ecological
speciation, diversification, trophic ecology, and community change
Field and natural history
Arthropod monitoring, island field campaigns, environmental sampling, invasive‑species surveys,
contamination‑aware workflows, and plant–arthropod interaction studies
Molecular biodiversity
eDNA/eRNA, metabarcoding, DNA and RNA extraction, PCR and qPCR, primer design, long‑amplicon and
marker‑based sequencing
Collections‑based
science
Legacy collections and biological repositories, archive‑derived DNA, retrospective biodiversity analysis, prospective
time‑capsule design, and voucher–sample–sequence traceability
Collection informatics
Voucher–sample–sequence traceability, repeat‑sampling frameworks, structured metadata, reproducible pipelines,
Git/GitHub, renv, Markdown, and Quarto
Quantitative ecology
R, tidyverse, ggplot2, multivariate community analysis, biodiversity time series, ecological networks, and
spatial‑data processing
Public scholarship
Invited and plenary talks; biodiversity activities for school, university, museum, elder‑care, and disability‑inclusive
